$comment: Documentation-coverage floor for #1241, read by scripts/docs-ratchet.mjs in the required `validate` job of harness-quality.yml. It is the BACKSTOP to the #865 merge-base identity rule, which fails a PR whose diff unlinks a documented file but cannot see dilution: PRs that each add only undocumented files are green under it forever while coverage walks down. Raise the floor when coverage rises; never lower it to make CI pass.
$whatCounts: harness check-docs (CLI 12.10.1, core checkDocCoverage) reads ONLY .md files under docsDir (./docs). A source file (**/*.{ts,js,tsx,jsx,mjs,cjs} under rootDir, minus entropy.excludePatterns) is documented when one of those files holds a markdown link [text](target) whose target, after stripping one leading ../ and then one leading ./, equals the file's repo-relative path (or src/ + that path), or whose target's basename equals the file's basename. So a link from a nested doc such as docs/a/b.md usually matches by basename only. Links in AGENTS.md, README.md, CHANGELOG.md or any other markdown outside docs/ are never read, and a backtick path is not a link: that is why scripts/schedule-staleness.mjs (PR #1235) reads as undocumented although AGENTS.md links it. The basename match also means one link to a common name (e.g. index.ts) documents every file of that name.
$metric: Coverage is measuredDocumented / measuredScanned * 100, computed from the report's file lists. harness prints Math.round of that ratio, so its '18.0%' is 17.86% here and would hide up to half a point of drift.
$headroom: minCoveragePercent sits maxHeadroom (1) point below the measurement, the same deliberate slack the entropy and perf ceilings carry. At 70 documented of 392 scanned that is 23 new undocumented files with no doc added in between: 70/415 = 16.87% passes, 70/416 = 16.83% fails. The headroom is a SHARED, ABSOLUTE budget that no branch can see the others spending: once it is spent, the next PR that adds an undocumented file fails, whoever wrote it. That PR links a file from docs/ (or links the new file); nobody lowers the floor. A floor pinned exactly to the measurement would spend the budget on day one and replay #864.
$restamp: The floor never moves on its own. When coverage rises more than maxHeadroom above the floor, the ratchet prints the values to write; commit them in a PR (chore(ratchet): restamp ...), measured in a clean worktree with the CLI the workflow resolves. A LOWERED floor is refused at runtime: on a pull request CI passes the merge base's copy of this file as --base-baseline, and the ratchet exits 1 when minCoveragePercent is below it, or 3 when the base copy cannot be read. Offline tests only check this file's self-consistency; a lowering with the headroom widened to match would pass them, which is why the rule lives in the ratchet.
$instrument: harnessCli is the EXACT version that measured this file. The workflow pins a floating @12, so the ratchet abstains (exit 3) when CI resolves a different version. Re-measure and update harnessCli in the same PR; do not delete it to silence the abstention.
$restamp3: 2026-11-12, the @13 -> @14 pin bump (13.0.0 -> 14.0.0): `harness check-docs --json --min-coverage 0` at origin/main 30e21eb7 in a fresh worktree outside the checkout, run side by side under explicitly pinned `@harness-engineering/cli@13.0.0` and `@14.0.0` in the same session: 87/457 documented under both, identical scalar fields and an identical 370-entry undocumented list, so CLI-independent across this major. The measured fields move 79/419 -> 87/457 because the CODE grew since 2026-10-23, not the instrument, and the floor moves 17.86 -> 18.04 because the ratchet's own nudge asked for exactly that restamp under 13.0.0 before this bump (1.18 points above the floor against 1 of allowed headroom). `harnessCli` bumped because a stale stamp abstains a passing gate.
$restamp2: 2026-10-21, the @12 -> @13 pin bump (12.10.1 -> 13.0.0): CLI-INDEPENDENT. Measured in a fresh worktree of origin/main 5d74d92c under both 12.10.1 and 13.0.0 with every consumed subcommand captured to a file: `harness check-docs --json` reads 75/414 on main under both CLIs; the bump branch reads 76/416. The floor moves up to the value docs-ratchet.mjs itself recommended (coverage sat 1.41 points above it, past maxHeadroom).
